title: Main purpose: profile of a person, work, or thing
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 23 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **23 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 7 Easy, 14 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question asks for the main purpose or overall purpose of the text, and every choice starts with 'To...'.
- The passage introduces an artist, activist, organization, invention, or phenomenon and gives facts or examples about it.
- There is no clear counterargument in the text.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Ask what every sentence has in common, since the purpose has to cover the whole text and not just its opening or last line.
- 2) Match the choice's verb to the tone: 'describe,' 'illustrate,' or 'provide examples of' fits neutral exposition, while 'argue' or 'criticize' needs an explicit opinion in the text.
- 3) Eliminate any choice that covers only one detail or introduces a comparison the text doesn't make.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Several choices name a detail that really is in the text, like one achievement, the founder's motive, or a single example, but that is too narrow to be the purpose.
Other choices use verbs that are too strong ('argue that X should be recognized') when the text only informs.
You pick a true detail instead of the purpose of the whole text.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Several choices name a detail that really is in the text, like one achievement, the founder's motive, or a single example, but that is too narrow to be the purpose.
Other choices use verbs that are too strong ('argue that X should be recognized') when the text only informs.
